messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Short data analyses
messages.body_plain:
Inacio and Marcio,
If you have data from a lab experiment that last only a couple of hours then the auto-calibration may not be successful because there will be limited data for this algorithm to train on. Your calibration results should confirm this. In https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27878845 we addressed this by using free-living data for the autocalibration.

In that case you set do.cal = FALSE and use calibration coefficients as separate input.

ENMO is not produced because there is no enough monitor wear time in a day. I think it is more logical to work with the epoch level data that is produced by part 1 directly and not use part 2 (or 3, 4, 5) for analysing experimental data that lasts only a couple of hours.

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Most computers would struggle to put all that data in memory and your screen will probably not have enough pixels to display all those numbers. This was one of the reasons why I developed GGIR: it loads and processes segments of the data and combines the results at the end to minimize memory requirements.
If you are keen to work with (segments of) the raw data directly then see package GENEAread.
Plotting of raw data in R is a lot quicker if you use argument type ="l" rather than the default type = "p".
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Taren,
The error message you get sounds to me as if the code still is trying to process part2 with 1 second epochs based on part 1 output with 5 second epochs.

I see you make multiple calls to g.shell.GGIR to run the different parts of the pipeline, which introduces a chance for accidental inconsistencies in function arguments... I cannot spot any inconsistencies but it is possible given the large amount of arguments there are. Further, I see you move the data to a different location, which introduces the risk of forgetting that old data still sits somewhere.

For testing purposes, have you tried simplifying the procedure by making only a single call to g.shell.GGIR with mode = c(1,2) to run part 1 and 2 sequentially? Preferably with a clean output folder to avoid confusion about which files are being processed and which output to look at.

Best,Vincent
